record.paper_title: Open problems in ageing science: A roadmap for biogerontology
record.original_question: In mammals, which molecular and cellular processes modulate the pace of ageing?

evidence.quote: What molecular and cellular processes modulate the pace of ageing in mammals?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Identify and characterize the molecular and cellular processes that modulate the pace of ageing in mammals. Specifically, determine which intracellular pathways (e.g., nutrient sensing, proteostasis, mitochondrial function, DNA damage response, epigenetic regulation), intercellular signaling mechanisms, and tissue-level processes (e.g., cellular senescence, stem-cell exhaustion, chronic inflammation) causally control the rate at which mammalian organisms accumulate age-related physiological decline. Provide, for each candidate process, evidence of its causal role in setting the ageing rate and quantitative relationships between its modulation and changes in lifespan or healthspan across mammalian species.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad biological grand-challenge question rather than a closed mathematical problem. While many candidate hallmarks of ageing have been proposed and partially validated (e.g., the well-known "hallmarks of ageing" framework by López-Otín et al., updated in 2023), no comprehensive, causal account of which processes set the pace of mammalian ageing exists, and the question is widely acknowledged as open in the biogerontology literature.

status_evidence.title: Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe (2023)
status_evidence.snippet: The updated hallmarks framework lists candidate processes (genomic instability, telomere attrition, epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, etc.) believed to modulate ageing, while noting causal contributions remain incompletely understood.
status_evidence.claim: The processes modulating mammalian ageing pace are still being catalogued and causally dissected, indicating the question remains open.
